why: Every command in both briefs runs as written. Builder: `npm test` works because package.json has "test":"node --test", and every file it names is tracked. Its execFileSync call with ['bin/csv2json.js','--tsv'] is a valid argument list for node. Verifier: the printf/node/od pipelines, `npm test; echo "exit=$?"` and `grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js` / README.md are all valid shell and use existing files and tools. The issue's proof uses `npm run test:cli`, which doesn't exist. The verifier catches this ("package.json has no such script") and uses `npm test` instead, so it never tells an agent to run the missing script. One weak spot: the optional advisory example `node bin/csv2json.js foo --tsv` pipes no stdin and may wait for input. It is only an "e.g." and not a required check, and it is still a valid command.
